value.body: A post-harvest engineer works on what happens to crops after harvest: cleaning, drying, grading, storage, cold chains and primary processing. Employers include agro-processing companies, cold-storage and warehousing firms, food processors and agri-equipment makers. Work is split between the plant or warehouse floor and planning equipment and layouts.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech Agricultural Engineering (processing and food engineering electives help)

items.label: Work areas
items.value: Drying and milling, cold storage, grading and packing, warehousing

items.label: Harvest and post-harvest losses
items.note: Range across crops in each group; reference period 2020-22
items.source: NABCONS study for the Ministry of Food Processing Industries (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Graduates join agro-processing plants, cold-chain operators and equipment makers as graduate engineer trainees, via campus placement or direct application. Internships in a processing plant or cold store strengthen an application.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Unit operations such as drying and milling

value.title: At a glance
items: Plants are often near production areas, away from big cities.
Next roles: production or plant engineer, cold-chain manager, or plant head.
Work can be seasonal around harvest peaks.
